assets.description: Revision 29 redraws engaged as a black silhouette of one armored warrior with a kabuto helmet, paired horn-shaped maedate crest, layered shikoro neck guard, broad sode shoulder armor, cuirass and kusazuri skirt plates. The warrior takes a bent-knee staggered stance and holds one upright straight-shafted su-yari with a simple spearhead in two separated hands aligned along the same shaft. The armor outline replaces the former jingasa figure. The background and broad negative spaces are transparent, with no plaque, pattern or frame. The complete 5:8 canvas retains measured transparent padding.

assets.description: Large dark-brown-and-muted-gold framed illustration of exactly one fallen aged-white sashimono. Revision 21 restores all interior cuts and holes, leaving a continuous intact white cloth panel with broad natural folds. Damage is confined to restrained missing corners, edge-connected tears and light white fraying around the outer perimeter; no burn marks or brown scorched rims. Broken rope-lashed timber palisades, collapsed rails and a little dry grass remain softly rendered in the background. No fire, smoke or embers. Transparent exterior; no second flag, hat, arrows, lettering or clan crest. The icon does not replace the unit affiliation flag.

Revision 29 replaces only the three engaged exports with a revised black armored-warrior silhouette on a transparent background: a kabuto helmet with a paired horn-shaped crest, layered shikoro neck guard, broad sode shoulder armor, cuirass and kusazuri, with one upright straight-shafted su-yari held in two separated hands along the same shaft. Use engaged.png (320x512) as the runtime texture, engaged-100x160.png as the display-size export and the 640x1024 source. Preserve the complete 5:8 canvas and transparent padding at 100x160, top-left (20,26), center (70,106). Replace only the hosted engaged texture and refresh its cache. The approved revision-28 out_of_command messenger is unchanged at 100x160, top-left (892,26), center (942,106); both header states can appear simultaneously. All other six asset objects and eighteen PNGs, and all six archived circular exports, are unchanged. The formation pair remains the transparent revision-26 artwork at its existing mutually exclusive candidate placement. All icon display sizes, placement guidance and unresolved placement questions remain unchanged. All seven cloud_url fields remain empty. Existing full-canvas title-bar clearances are retained; TTS runtime rendering, front/back display, distance, angle and operation-area overlap remain unverified.
notes: Revision 29 changes only engaged: the former jingasa spear figure is replaced by a black armored-warrior silhouette with a kabuto helmet, paired horn-shaped maedate crest, layered shikoro neck guard, broad sode shoulder armor, cuirass and kusazuri. The warrior takes a bent-knee staggered stance. One upright straight-shafted su-yari is held in two separated hands aligned along the same shaft. The transparent background and complete 5:8 canvas are retained. The approved revision-28 out_of_command messenger, including its question mark, remains unchanged.

All three revision-29 engaged PNGs were remeasured for RGBA mode, pixel dimensions, alpha>0 and alpha>=128 bounds, transparent padding and SHA-256. Alpha and visible-pixel RGB values are recorded from each export; the former revision-28 measurements are superseded for engaged. Measured alpha range and visible RGB minimum to maximum in R/G/B order: engaged.png alpha [0, 254], RGB [0, 0, 0] to [3, 3, 2]; 源图/engaged-640x1024.png alpha [0, 255], RGB [0, 0, 0] to [4, 3, 3]; engaged-100x160.png alpha [0, 254], RGB [0, 0, 0] to [1, 2, 1]. The generated figure was scaled proportionally with Box area downsampling to fit within 608x960, centered on a transparent 640x1024 source canvas, then exported at 320x512 and 100x160. Alpha was not normalized.

Header runtime textures remain engaged.png and out_of_command.png at 320x512; display-size exports remain 100x160 and sources remain 640x1024 at their existing paths. Preserve each complete 5:8 canvas and transparent padding at 100x160; do not crop to the visible silhouette bounds. Replace only the hosted engaged texture and refresh its cache for revision 29; keep the approved messenger texture. Integrations still using pre-revision-24 square artwork require UI height 100 to 160 and top-left y 56 to 26, keeping the existing centers; replace the old square artwork with the current files.

The other six asset objects (out_of_command, formation_close, formation_open, routed, fire_ready and fire_loading) and their eighteen PNG bytes match revision-28 commit cd2a3f90b46ed7fb7223899d625f402e1caf9592, as do all six archived circular exports. Display sizes, positions and remaining placement questions are unchanged for every icon. No new state triggers, reset rules or code changes are introduced.

Attempts to verify new museum/object-image references at The Met, British Museum and Wikimedia Commons were blocked by HTTP CONNECT 403. No reference object images were downloaded for this revision, and this drawing does not claim a verified historical reconstruction.

Historical revision 28 replaced both header plaques with black figure silhouettes. Its engaged used a jingasa-wearing spear figure; revision 29 supersedes that figure with an armored warrior and a straight shaft. The revision-28 paused messenger looking back to the left, outward-reaching right hand, rolled message at the waist and bold question mark remain the approved out_of_command artwork.

Historical revision 28 measured all six then-current header exports and used proportional Box area downsampling to fit silhouettes within 608x960 before centering on transparent 640x1024 source canvases; alpha was not normalized. Those historical engaged files and measurements are superseded in revision 29. The messenger files and their metadata remain unchanged.

Historical revision 27 placed the natural steel crossed swords and the charcoal gunbai with its black prohibition circle and slash on warm-ivory opaque rectangular plaques. Those plaques had thick dark-brown straight-corner frames, narrow muted-gold inner lines and restrained pale-gold Japanese cloud motifs in the corners and along the sides. Revision 28 removes the plaques and replaces both motifs with black figure silhouettes.

Historical revision 27 header exports were fully opaque RGBA with alpha 255 throughout each canvas, full-canvas bounds at both alpha thresholds and zero transparent padding. Those alpha measurements belong to the former plaque files; current silhouette bounds, padding and hashes are recorded in the two asset objects.

Historical revision 26 removed the formation_close and formation_open paper plaques and dark-brown frames, leaving six isolated dark jingasa markers per icon. One transparent jingasa cutout was repeated six times in each established tight or loose/staggered arrangement at a matched marker scale. This transparent formation artwork remains current and is unchanged in revision 29; the two complete alpha masks and outer padding differ.

Use formation_close.png and formation_open.png (512x256) as preferred runtime textures, with 240x120 display exports and 1024x512 sources. Keep the full 2:1 canvas at 240x120 at the existing shared candidate top-left (734,1042), center (854,1102). The states remain mutually exclusive. Do not crop transparent margins or enlarge the close-packed cluster to fill its canvas; that would change the shared marker scale and placement.

Historical revision 26 remeasured all six formation exports for RGBA mode, pixel dimensions, alpha>0 and alpha>=128 bounds, transparent padding and SHA-256. Generation alpha was normalized over 6.25%-93.75% to remove faint background residue and exports used Box area downsampling.

Historical revision 26 source-image component check at alpha>=128 found exactly six disconnected jingasa components in each 1024x512 source, each with a 146x140 bounding box and 15906 pixels. The same transparent cutout gives matched scale across both arrangements. The artwork was reconstructed with approximately 1-2px scale normalization, not preserved pixel-for-pixel from the former plaques.

Historical revision 25 changed engaged to natural cool-gray/silver steel blades, dark cord-wrapped handles, dark-iron guards and subdued old-brass/bronze fittings. Revision 27 retained that crossed-katana motif on a decorated opaque plaque. Revision 28 replaces the entire motif and plaque with a black warrior silhouette; the 5:8 canvas, 100x160 display size and placement are retained.

Historical revision 24 replaced engaged and out_of_command circular badges with transparent motif-only artwork. Its engaged had ivory blades and light guard accents, superseded by natural material colors in revision 25. Revision 24 introduced the charcoal gunbai with a thick black hollow prohibition circle and slash, narrow ivory outlines and a handle below the ring. Revision 27 added decorated opaque plaques to those motifs; revision 28 supersedes both motifs and plaques with black figure silhouettes. Revision 24 established the 5:8 canvases and 100x160 header placements retained today.

The engaged silhouette uses a 100x160 canvas at (20,26), centered at (70,106). The out_of_command silhouette uses a separate 100x160 canvas at (892,26), centered at (942,106). Both can appear simultaneously; do not reuse one mutually exclusive display slot.

The title-bar interior is x=[14,998), y=[14,198). All 12 saved title alpha bounds and placement metadata were checked for the established full-canvas placement. The tightest titles, 鉄砲足軽隊 and 鉄砲僧兵隊, occupy x=[128,885). Full-canvas clearance remains 8px to the left canvas, 7px to the right canvas, 6px to each corresponding side frame, and 12px above and below both canvases. No title needs to move or shrink; the existing 96 cards are unchanged.

Historical circular exports are archived only in 历史/圆章-revision23/: engaged.png, engaged-100.png, engaged-1024.png, out_of_command.png, out_of_command-100.png and out_of_command-1024.png. They are not current runtime textures. Old source and display-size paths must be migrated to the new rectangular-canvas exports.

Historical revision 10 cleaned the circular alpha boundary and added matching dark outer lines and matte pale-gold bands. Historical revision 12 changed the gunbai slash to ivory with a dark-brown outline. Those circle styles, their 512x512 runtime textures, 100x100 placement and uniform circular padding are superseded by revision 24; archived images document them only.

fire_ready.png and fire_loading.png are the preferred 512x256 runtime textures; the corresponding -240x120.png files are display-size convenience exports; both sources are 1024x512. Use the full canvases at 240x120 without trimming transparent padding. The pair shares one mutually exclusive shooting-status slot; no placement coordinates, new state triggers or reset rules are assigned.

Historical revision 23 changes only fire_loading: an enlarged muzzle-and-light-wooden-ramrod close-up crops out the stock and breech, and one prominent ivory slash with a deep-brown outline descends opposite the barrel to make loading/unavailable to fire distinct. The muzzle-ramrod junction remains uncovered; there is no hand. Matte ivory plaque styling, all canvas dimensions and exterior alpha boundaries are retained. The other six asset objects and their eighteen PNGs are unchanged.

Historical revision 22 introduced fire_ready and fire_loading as matte ivory plaques with dark-brown borders. fire_ready showed a horizontal complete Japanese tanegashima; the original fire_loading showed a raised complete musket with a lighter wooden ramrod inserted into the muzzle and no hand. Revision 23 supersedes that loading composition; fire_ready remains unchanged.

Historical revision 21 repairs every interior routed cloth slit and puncture. Only perimeter tears, missing corners and restrained white fraying remain. Natural folds, the soft palisade background, single fallen white banner and frame are retained. The other four asset entries and their PNGs are unchanged; all display-size and placement guidance is unchanged.

routed.png is 1200x800, routed-600x400.png is the display-size export, and the source is 1536x1024. Candidate display size is 600x400 on a 1200x1200 board; no coordinates or automatic elevation logic are assigned. The rounded alpha outline removes outside background remnants; Box area downsampling retains a narrow antialiased edge.

Revision 21 generated no new preview or overview image; its overview reference pointed to standalone routed.png. Commander overlap, front/back rendering, distance and oblique-angle readability still require code-side and TTS validation; the artwork alone does not prevent occlusion.

Historical revision 11 made the ivory formation plaques taller and increased vertical row spacing in formation_open. The matching plaque alpha boundaries and 240x120 visible plaque heights belonged to that former background. Revision 26 removes the plaques and frames while retaining six markers, the 2:1 canvases and the existing mutually exclusive candidate placement.

All earlier engaged, out_of_command and combined previews are historical and do not represent the current artwork. Revision 29 generated no new preview or overview image; overview remains the existing standalone formation_close.png. TTS runtime, front/back rendering, distance, angle, all-troop occlusion and operation-area overlap remain unverified.
Cloud URLs intentionally empty; no runtime-hosting URLs have been provided.

At a 300px-wide board each 100x160 header placement becomes approximately 25x40px; the rectangular canvas fit does not establish TTS edge clarity or readability. Final appearance requires TTS distance and angle testing.
Back previews are charcoal contrast/layout illustrations, not captured or reconstructed TTS backs.
This handoff defines artwork and placement only, not automatic state detection, timing, persistence, or reset rules.
